page: Microsoft Azure E16_v3 is an Ev3-family virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8171M processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1D cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It also includes 410 GB of local SSD storage, while offering zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core CPU, single-threaded gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core scores all falling into the bottom 10% of tested systems. Multi-threaded performance is more robust, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores landing in the average category (middle 50%). Memory bandwidth is also average, reaching 610.2 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 71.84 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database and web operations perform at an average tier, with Redis SET operations achieving 10.12 million operations per second and static web serving throughput reaching 9.85 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the E16_v3 is its weak single-threaded execution speed, making it less suitable for latency-sensitive, single-core bound tasks or heavy LLM inference on medium-to-large models. However, its high memory density of 128 GB and bundled 410 GB local SSD provide a cost-effective profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require cutting-edge CPU speeds. It is well-suited for relational databases, caching layers like Redis, software compilation, and general-purpose multi-threaded enterprise applications.
description: Microsoft Azure E16_v3 is an Ev3-family virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing a memory-optimized 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8171M processor running at 2.6 GHz, the system includes 410 GB of local SSD storage. Performance benchmarks indicate a clear tradeoff: single-core execution is weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core capabilities, memory bandwidth, and database operations perform in the average tier, with Redis SET operations reaching 10.12 million operations per second. Lacking a GPU, this instance is not designed for heavy AI acceleration but offers a balanced, memory-dense profile. It is best suited for memory-intensive workloads, database management, caching layers, and multi-threaded enterprise applications where high memory capacity is prioritized over raw single-threaded CPU speed.
